conviction_note: Small lean down. Retail-channel peers that reported after LZB's 19 Aug call were soft. NRF furniture was -2.7% YoY in Sep and -2.6% in Oct; Havertys Aug-Sep written was +1.7% with a flat Labor Day; Ethan Allen retail written was -1.2% for Jul-Sep and +0.3% in Oct. LZB also missed both Q1 guide lines, even with a 240bp tariff/refund tailwind, and warned that friction costs persist. Against that, wholesale upholstery peers' orders were up (Flexsteel +5%, Bassett domestic upholstery double-digit), the year-ago written same-store compare was -2%, and the put skew (+15 vol pts) and the -17% Q1 reaction already price the downside. So p_up 47 on a 12-point absolute move, giving -0.72 against a findings sum of -0.9. The two agree in sign and roughly in size.
bar: Company guide FQ2 FY27 (quarter ended ~24 Oct 2026): sales $500-520M, adjusted operating margin 4.0-5.5% (SEC 8-K ex-99, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000057131/000005713126000034/fy27q1pressrelease.htm). Consensus: adj EPS $0.48 and revenue $507.9M (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-11-10, https://finviz.com/news/420664/la-z-boys-retail-revival-faces-a-margin-test-as-wholesale-softness-lingers). Benzinga carries $0.48 / $506.9M and FXEmpire/Chartmill $0.48 / $511.7M, so EPS agrees across three sources and revenue sits in a $506.6-511.7M band in the lower half of the guide. The whisper equals consensus. Year-ago: $0.71 on $522.5M, adj op margin 7.1%, which included a 110bp one-time warranty benefit. Revenue consensus fell from ~$537M when the guide was issued to ~$508M now.
positioning_check: Short interest 2,027,808 shares, 5.1% of shares outstanding, 4.05 days to cover, FINRA settlement 2026-10-30 (https://equibles.com/stocks/lzb/short-interest). That is down from 2.09M on 10-15 but up from 1.53M before the Q1 print (+417k into the 08-31 settlement). Not crowded, so no squeeze mechanism of note. Options (baseline): 25d skew +15.11 vol pts, i.e. downside paid; event-implied move 10.98%; put/call OI 1.02 on only 724 contracts total. Tape: 20d run-up +6.6%, 5d -4.7%, 26% below the 52-week high and 8.5% above the low. The Earnings Whispers preview says bullish sentiment fell to 38% from 47.5% before the last report.

findings.finding: Retail-channel demand data published after LZB last spoke (19 Aug) was soft. CNBC/NRF Retail Monitor furniture & home furnishings was -2.7% YoY in Sep 2026 and -2.62% in Oct 2026, the only declining category. Havertys (reported 4 Nov) saw comp written +2.3% for Jul-Sep, slowing from +12.3% in Q2, with Aug-Sep written +1.7% and a flat Labor Day. Ethan Allen (reported 9 Nov) saw retail written orders -1.2% YoY for Jul-Sep and +0.3% in October. The bar implicitly needs LZB's written same-store to stay positive after Q1's +3%; this data argues it slowed. LZB's fiscal Q2 runs late July to 24 Oct and spans Labor Day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Written same-store is the line management leads with. Q2 FY26 (Nov 2025) had written same-store -2% with 'October the strongest month' plus a margin beat and gained +20.2%. Q1 FY27 (Aug 2026) had written same-store +3% but missed on sales and margin and fell -17%. So comps alone have not set the sign; margin and the guide did.
findings.why_not_priced: Revenue consensus has already drifted to the lower half of the guide ($508M vs $500-520M), so some softness is priced. But the EPS bar ($0.48) sits at the guide midpoint margin, and the whisper equals consensus. If the market had priced a comp slowdown to flat or negative, the EPS bar or the whisper would sit below mid-guide.
findings.independence: Three sources: NRF series (https://nrf.com/media-center/press-releases/cnbc-nrf-retail-monitor-shows-12th-month-of-sales-growth-in-september), Havertys Q3 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000216085/000162828026069778/ex991-hvtearningsreleasex3.htm), Ethan Allen Q1 FY27 release (https://finviz.com/news/419436/ethan-allen-reports-first-quarter-results). Counter-evidence: Wayfair called the category 'roughly flat' with US revenue +11.4% (https://finviz.com/news/415205/wayfair-announces-third-quarter-2026-results-reports-double-digit-us-revenue-growth), Arhaus comp written was +13.9%, and Bassett's full Labor Day event written was +9%. These share-gainers' figures are why this is sized small. Proxy, not LZB's own number.

findings.finding: The year-ago written same-store compare is easy. In FQ2 FY26 LZB's retail written same-store was -2%, against +3% in FQ1 FY27, which management said strengthened sequentially. So a flat-to-modest positive comp is attainable even in a soft category. LZB also added 32 company-owned stores over the 12 months to Q1, so total retail written growth runs well above same-store.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same as above: the comp line has not decided the sign on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: Public, so largely priced. It is filed because it partially offsets the peer softness above. It would be visible if consensus revenue sat at or above guide midpoint, and it does not.
findings.independence: Q1 FY27 SEC release confirms written same-store +3%, retail written +16%, and 32 stores added (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000057131/000005713126000034/fy27q1pressrelease.htm; https://finviz.com/news/403065/la-z-boy-incorporated-announces-additional-new-store-openings-and-acquisitions).

findings.finding: Wholesale upholstery peers reporting since LZB's Q1 call showed order growth. Flexsteel (Jul-Sep) orders were about +5%, backlog +8.2% to $77.7M, and it guides Oct-Dec sales +3.5-6.5% ex-exit. Bassett (Jun-Aug) wholesale orders were +7.9%, with double-digit domestic upholstery. Hooker domestic upholstery backlog was +4.8%. LZB itself said 'wholesale demand patterns improved throughout the first quarter and backlog is solid entering the second quarter'. LZB wholesale is ~65% of Q1 sales ($323M), down 5% ex-divestiture in Q1. A US-made upholstery maker also benefits from the 25% Section 232 duty on imported upholstery.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q1 FY27 wholesale -9% (-5% ex-divestiture) with margin falling to 6.8% from 7.5% was a core part of the -17% reaction. Wholesale volume deleverage is the margin swing factor.
findings.why_not_priced: The Earnings Whispers preview frames wholesale as 'softness lingers' with 'orders would stay uneven'. If the market priced the peer order turn, revenue consensus would not have fallen to the lower half of the guide.
findings.independence: Bassett FQ3 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000010329/000143774926031601/ex_1020960.htm), Hooker Q2 FY27 (https://pulse2.com/hooker-furnishings-returns-to-q2-profitability-with-1-7-million-net-income-and-7-9-million-in-tariff-recoveries/), and LZB's own Q1 release on backlog (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000057131/000005713126000034/fy27q1pressrelease.htm). Counter: on the Q1 call LZB said it expects wholesale 'choppiness to continue' and noted deeper wholesale discounting. Peer proxy.

findings.finding: Q1 FY27 execution argues the 4.0-5.5% Q2 margin guide is at risk. Q1 printed sales of $476M against a $490-510M guide and 3.9% adj op margin against a 4.0-5.5% guide, missing both lines below the low end. That margin already included a 240bp favorable tariff impact (IEEPA refunds plus pricing), so the underlying margin was ~1.5%. On the call management said the three parallel supply-chain projects carry 'incremental friction cost versus expectations, which we expect to remain for the balance of the year.' Q2 also loses the year-ago 110bp warranty benefit, though that is already in the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin vs guide has set the sign. Q1 FY27 missed both lines and fell -16.95%. Q2 FY26 beat (7.1% margin 'exceeded internal expectations', $0.71 vs $0.54) and rose +20.21%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock fell 17% on Q1 and puts are bid. But consensus EPS of $0.48 sits exactly at mid-guide margin, so the Street is giving full credit to a guide the company missed last quarter. Pricing the repeat-miss risk would put the bar near the low end (~$0.40).
findings.independence: Q4 FY26 release shows the Q1 guide of $490-510M / 4.0-5.5% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000057131/000005713126000018/fy26q4pressrelease.htm). Q1 actuals in the SEC release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000057131/000005713126000034/fy27q1pressrelease.htm). Both are LZB's own documents, and their inference is one finding.

findings.finding: IEEPA tariff refunds may add to Q2 margin. Q1's adjusted margin included refunds within a 240bp tariff tailwind. Management says its refunds are 'significantly less than others in our industry' and are 'still in process', and peers booked material refunds in Jul-Sep (Hooker $7.9M, Bassett $2.8M, Arhaus ~$6M). Any LZB recognition in Q2 lifts reported adjusted margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q1 FY27 the tariff/refund tailwind was in the number and the stock still fell 17%. Peer reactions to refunds split on guidance (LESSONS #2).
findings.why_not_priced: Small and one-off. Analysts may already exclude it ('import-duty refunds that are smaller than those of rivals' is in the EW preview), so most of it is priced or ignored.
findings.independence: Shares a document with the margin-guide finding (same call). Peer refunds come from https://pulse2.com/hooker-furnishings-returns-to-q2-profitability-with-1-7-million-net-income-and-7-9-million-in-tariff-recoveries/ and the Bassett 8-K.

findings.finding: Robert Sundy II, President of Retail, sold 5,000 shares on 2026-09-10 at a ~$30.85 weighted average, about 8% of his holding (59,297 after), mid-quarter and with no 10b5-1 plan stated. Director Janet Kerr's 3,653-share sale on 09-08 was under a 10b5-1 plan. No insider buys after the 17% drop.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history; insider sales at LZB are routine but usually at higher prices (June 2026 sales at ~$41).
findings.why_not_priced: Small Form 4 on an under-followed name. The retail head selling near the 52-week low, in the third week of the quarter he runs, is a weak tell on retail written trends. It would be priced if retail comp expectations had been cut, and they have not.

findings.finding: Joybird (DTC e-commerce) written sales were -17% in Q1 with delivered $27M, and management expects it to remain a drag in Q2 while moving manufacturing into US plants by fiscal year-end. This is a drag inside the guided range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Joybird took a $20M goodwill impairment in Q4 FY26 and the stock rose +14.8% on that print, so this line has not moved the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside guidance and public, so mostly priced. Filed for completeness.
findings.independence: Same company document as the Q1 facts.

outside_window.finding: The Section 232 duty on imported upholstered furniture is scheduled to rise from 25% to 30% on 2027-01-01 (deferred by the 2025-12-31 proclamation). That is a structural tailwind for LZB's ~90% US-made upholstery. It may colour the FQ3 guide, but the rate change itself lands after the window.
FINRA short interest for the 2026-11-13 settlement (model estimate +7.4%) is published 2026-11-24, after the window.

baseline_tension: The small negative lean agrees with the +15 vol-pt put skew and the post-Q1 drawdown, so most of it is probably priced. The positive wholesale-order evidence cuts against the skew, which is why p_up sits close to 50 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: #7/#1 (the sign agrees with a strong skew and the Q1 miss is already in the -17% reaction): margin-guide-risk finding cut from -1.5 to -1.0; p_up moved from 46 to 47.

#6 (inside guidance): Joybird drag cut from -0.2 to -0.1. Easy-compare finding cut from +0.5 to +0.4 as largely public.
